title: Bible Camps — Determining if Property is Exempt
summary: Decision tree for whether Bible camp property is exempt under sec. 70.11(11): Property Tax Exemption Request (Form PR-230) filing, 40-acre exemption limit, religious nonprofit corporation ownership, religious-purpose use, and pecuniary profit.
disclaimer: This flow chart provides general information and may not apply in every situation. A thorough review of each property is still required.
router_description: Bible camp property tax exemption under sec. 70.11(11). Specifically for a Bible camp or religious summer camp owned by a religious nonprofit corporation, with a 40-acre exemption limit. This is the narrow camp exemption only; it does NOT cover ordinary churches, houses of worship, or the general religious-use exemption under sec. 70.11(4).

nodes.question: Was the "Property Tax Exemption Request", form PR-230, filed with the municipal assessor where the property is located by March 1?

authorities.note: must be filed with the municipal assessor by March 1

nodes.question: Does the property exceed 40 acres?
nodes.note: The law limits the exemption to 40 acres. Acreage above 40 is taxable. See page 19-7 of the WPAM.

nodes.question: Is the property owned by a religious nonprofit corporation organized under Wisconsin laws?
Is the property used for religious purposes?
nodes.note: See WPAM pages 19-13 to 19-14 and the discussion of religious institutions.

nodes.question: Is the property used for pecuniary profit of any individual?
